chapter_name: The World Population Distribution Density and Growth
learning_objective: 🎯 Explore how people are spread unevenly across the globe, the factors influencing where they live, and how populations grow and change!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Population is distributed very unevenly. Roughly 90% of the world's population lives in about 10% of its land area.
Density is the ratio between people and land. It is calculated by dividing total population by total land area (Persons per sq km).
People settle based on geographical factors (water availability, landforms, climate), economic factors (minerals, urbanization, industries), and social/cultural factors.
Population changes due to three main factors: Births (Crude Birth Rate), Deaths (Crude Death Rate), and Migration (In-migration and Out-migration).
A model showing how a society's population changes from high birth and death rates (agrarian society) to low birth and death rates (urban-industrial society) as it develops.

fun_activity.title: 🌎 The Crowded Room
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine a room with 100 chairs representing the world's land. In reality, 60 people would be fighting for just 6 chairs in 'Asia', while 1 person would have an entire chair to themselves in 'Oceania'!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the formula for Population Density: Density = Total Population ÷ Total Area.
📌 Differentiate clearly between Push factors (reasons to leave a place, like war or poverty) and Pull factors (reasons to go to a place, like jobs or peace).
📌 Be prepared to draw and label the 3 stages of the Demographic Transition Model.
quick_recap: ⭐ Asia is the most populated continent, possessing many of the most densely populated countries.
⭐ Water availability and pleasant climates are the strongest physical pull factors for human settlement.
⭐ The difference between births and deaths provides the 'natural growth' of a population.
